rationale: Available literature from the initial discovery cohort (Ramond et al., 2023) and curated disease records (OMIM #621421) confirms that while developmental delay/intellectual disability is universally observed (12/12 affected individuals), feeding difficulties are classified as 'frequently associated' or 'more variable features'. Consequently, early feeding difficulties are not an obligate diagnostic criterion, and their absence does not rule out Ramond-Elliott neurodevelopmental syndrome in patients presenting with developmental delay, microcephaly, and infantile spasms.

evidence.text: In the index cohort characterizing Ramond-Elliott syndrome across 12 individuals from 11 unrelated families, all patients exhibited intellectual disability and/or developmental delay, whereas feeding difficulties, infantile spasms, microcephaly, brain anomalies, autism spectrum disorder, and short stature were described as frequently associated rather than universally present.

source.title: Clustered variants in the 5' coding region of TRA2B cause a distinctive neurodevelopmental syndrome
source.quote: All affected individuals presented intellectual disability and/or developmental delay, frequently associated with infantile spasms, microcephaly, brain anomalies, autism spectrum disorder, feeding difficulties, and short stature.

evidence.text: OMIM entry #621421 explicitly groups feeding difficulties alongside poor overall growth and dysmorphic facial features under the designation of 'more variable features' rather than core obligate manifestations.

source.title: 621421 - RAMOND-ELLIOTT NEURODEVELOPMENTAL SYNDROME; RAMELN
source.quote: More variable features include poor overall growth, dysmorphic facial features, feeding difficulties

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact penetrance and clinical resolution of feeding difficulties (e.g., tube dependence vs. transient neonatal sucking weakness) in an expanded international cohort of TRA2B variant carriers?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying specific sub-phenotypes of feeding dysfunction across developmental stages will determine whether transient feeding difficulties were subclinically present or truly absent in atypical/milder presentations.

new_directions.question_text: Does the presence or severity of feeding difficulties correlate with the specific alternative start codon usage or Tra2beta-3 isoform expression levels across different 5' TRA2B variants?
new_directions.rationale: Determining genotype-phenotype correlations could explain why some patients present with severe gastrointestinal/swallowing dysfunction while others completely spare feeding.
